description: pkix-chain/src/lib.rs:527-552: The two-tier verify_one design (try validate_path on caller chain first, only fall through to AIA on is_aia_recoverable) is the right shape. It preserves zero-cost behaviour for complete chains, surfaces non-recoverable cert defects (expired, KU wrong, etc.) directly without ever invoking the AIA seam, and bounds the slow-path cost to genuine missing-intermediate cases. A naive design would always go through path_builder; that would force a needless CertPool construction on every verify call. A future contributor might suggest 'simplify by always going through build_first_valid_path' — defend the split: the fast path is the steady-state for callers who supply complete chains (the documented best practice), and bypassing the builder there is a documented optimization, not premature.
title: Fast-path / slow-path split in Verifier::verify_one — preserve
